expectations.text: States plainly that the not-empty check is insufficient
expectations.evidence: "Your new test would have been green every single day of the outage."

expectations.text: Identifies the COALESCE to zero as the mechanism that made the failure silent
expectations.evidence: "COALESCE(revenue, 0) converts 'we don't know' into 'we know, it's zero' — the data equivalent of except: pass. Zero is a plausible business value, so it can never look wrong."

expectations.text: Recommends reconciliation against a source of truth, not only shape checks
expectations.evidence: "Warehouse total vs. billing/Stripe source total. This is the one."

expectations.text: Recommends that assertions run before publication rather than after, so bad data cannot reach the dashboard
expectations.evidence: "Assert between load and publish, not after. Build to staging → run assertions → promote on pass."

expectations.text: Recommends a data contract or schema check so an upstream rename fails loudly and attributably
expectations.evidence: "A contract at the ingest boundary — assert expected columns exist before the model runs — turns a rename from three silent weeks into a red build in one run, attributable to the upstream team."

expectations.text: Recommends volume or null-rate assertions rather than only a non-empty check
expectations.evidence: "null rate on revenue jumping 0% → 100% on day one, yes... assert null_rate = 0 on the joined key."

expectations.text: Treats three weeks of nobody noticing as a detection gap worth its own fix
expectations.evidence: Uses the three-week period as evidence in the table but does not explicitly treat it as a detection gap worth its own fix; frames the insight around testing methodology instead

expectations.text: Explains why a silently wrong number is more dangerous than a failed pipeline
expectations.evidence: "COALESCE(revenue, 0) converts 'we don't know'... Zero is a plausible business value, so it can never look wrong."
